title: IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference (URTC) 2027
organizer_blurb: A student-run committee at MIT that organizes URTC with IEEE and the IEEE Boston Section.
summary: An annual research conference run by and for undergraduates, focused on engineering and technology research. Held at MIT's Stata Center in Cambridge.
description: URTC gives undergraduates a peer-reviewed venue for their engineering and computing research. Students can submit a technical paper, a poster, or a lightning talk; accepted work is presented over a weekend at the Stata Center, with awards for best paper, best poster and best lightning talk. Themes have spanned computation, automation, networks, sustainability and more. For the 2026 cycle, paper submissions closed in early August and poster and lightning talk submissions in early September, with reviews handled through Microsoft CMT. Even without submitting, attending is a good way to see what undergraduate research looks like and meet students from other schools.
location: Cambridge, MA
dates_note: The site lists Oct 8-10, 2027. 2027 submission deadlines are not posted; in 2026 papers were due Aug 9 (extended) and posters and lightning talks Sept 4.
eligibility: Described as a conference for and by undergraduates presenting undergraduate research. No formal eligibility rules are listed.

title: Stanford Research Conference (SRC) 2027
organizer_blurb: A Stanford student organization that promotes undergraduate research and hosts a national conference each spring.
summary: A spring conference at Stanford where undergraduates from across the country present research in any field, including computer science.
description: SRC is a student-run, multidisciplinary undergraduate research conference held on Stanford's campus, usually on the first or second weekend of Stanford's spring quarter. About 100 students present each year at poster sessions, and the weekend also includes workshops, keynotes, speaker panels and social events. The 2026 edition had over 120 attendees and 101 projects. Applications open in the fall, and an online info session has been held in December. Presenters who opt in get free on-campus hosting with a Stanford undergraduate, and a separate financial aid application is available, though not every applicant receives aid.
location: Stanford, CA
dates_note: 2027 dates not yet announced; SRC 2026 ran Apr 10-12, 2026. Applications open each fall, so check the site this fall.
pay: Free on-campus hosting for attendees who opt in; financial aid available by application
eligibility: All undergraduates enrolled at two- and four-year institutions may apply. Projects should be mostly completed during undergraduate study.

title: IEEE High Performance Extreme Computing Conference (HPEC) 2027
organizer_blurb: A long-running IEEE Boston Section conference on high performance and embedded computing.
summary: A virtual IEEE conference on high performance and embedded computing, organized from the Boston area. Student rates and a free attendance option have been offered.
description: HPEC is an IEEE conference on high performance and embedded computing, organized through the IEEE Boston Section. Recent editions have been fully virtual, running over a week in September on an online event platform that registered attendees log into. Students can follow sessions remotely, and undergraduates have presented papers there. The 2026 site advertised student rates and a complimentary attendance option, which makes it an easy, low-cost way to sample an IEEE technical conference.
dates_note: 2027 dates not yet announced; the 30th edition ran virtually Sept 14-18, 2026. Check the site's future dates page in spring.
pay: Student rates and a complimentary option were offered in 2026

title: NSBE 53rd Annual Convention 2027
organizer_blurb: One of the largest student-governed engineering organizations in the US, supporting Black engineers and technologists.
summary: NSBE's national convention comes to Boston in 2027, with a large career expo, technical competitions and professional development sessions.
description: The NSBE Annual Convention is a multi-day gathering of collegiate and professional members with workshops, plenaries, panels, tech and science competitions, awards and a large career and innovation expo where employers recruit for internships and full-time roles. The 2026 convention drew more than 13,000 participants, and organizers expect over 16,000 in Boston. The 2027 theme is Engineered with Intention. Being in Boston makes this unusually reachable for Suffolk students. Registration opens in fall 2026, the full agenda is expected in February 2027, and member rates depend on an active NSBE membership.
location: Boston, MA (Thomas M. Menino Convention & Exhibition Center)
dates_note: Registration opens in fall 2026 (the site says October in one place and November in another).
eligibility: Collegiate and professional rates are tied to an active NSBE membership; APEx rates also require a verified GPA.

title: Harvard WECode 2027
organizer: Harvard Undergraduate Women in Computer Science
organizer_blurb: A Harvard undergraduate group that has run the WECode conference for women in tech since 2014.
summary: A student-run weekend conference at Harvard for women in computing and STEM, with industry speakers, mentorship and networking.
description: WECode is a large student-run conference for women in tech, organized by Harvard undergraduates. The weekend features keynotes from industry leaders, workshops, mentorship circles and networking, plus pre-conference events, a tech fellows program, and scholarships and housing support listed on the site. It draws attendees from many colleges, and past editions have also offered a virtual ticket. It is a short trip from Suffolk and a strong option for students looking to build community and meet recruiters.
location: Cambridge, MA
dates_note: The site lists Feb 19-20, 2027; venue and 2027 ticket prices are not posted yet. The 2026 edition ran Feb 21-22 at Harvard.
eligibility: Aimed at women in STEM fields. No other requirements are stated.

title: Boston Code Camp 41
organizer_blurb: An all-volunteer community event that has run developer code camps in Greater Boston for many years.
summary: A free one-day developer conference in Burlington with talks from local engineers on software, cloud and AI topics.
description: Boston Code Camp is a free, one-day Saturday community conference where local developers, designers and companies share what they work on. Sessions are given by regional and local speakers, including Microsoft developer experts and MVPs. Students can attend talks, network with working engineers, and, in future editions, submit a session through the Sessionize call for speakers. Bring a photo ID, since the host building requires one at entry.
location: Burlington, MA (Microsoft Sales & Technology Center)
dates_note: The call for speakers closes Oct 17, 2026. Code Camp usually runs twice a year (Code Camp 40 was in March 2026).
eligibility: Open to the public; no eligibility rules are stated.

title: BSides CambridgeMA 2026
organizer_blurb: A community-organized local chapter of the BSides security conference series.
summary: A free, one-day community hacker conference in Somerville for security practitioners, newcomers and tech enthusiasts.
description: BSides CambridgeMA is a sponsor-funded, community-run security conference held on a Sunday morning and early afternoon. Talks come from local community members and focus on practical security research, vulnerability discovery and ethical hacking, with no sponsored talks. It is a low-cost, low-pressure first security conference for students interested in cybersecurity. The venue is reachable from Davis Square on the Red Line or Magoun Square on the Green Line.
location: Somerville, MA (Center for Arts at the Armory)
dates_note: Runs about 8:30 AM to 1:45 PM. Registration is open; the call for proposals closed Aug 3, 2026.
eligibility: Open to all; registration required.

title: SIGCSE Virtual 2026
organizer_blurb: The ACM Special Interest Group on Computer Science Education.
summary: A fully online ACM conference on computing education, held every other year in the fall.
description: SIGCSE Virtual is the online-only sibling of the SIGCSE Technical Symposium, focused on how computing is taught and learned. Tracks include papers, posters, panels, tutorials, special sessions, working groups, birds-of-a-feather sessions and a doctoral consortium. All attendance is remote, so students interested in teaching, tutoring or CS education research can join without travel. The organizers were also recruiting volunteers for committees and reviewing.
dates_note: Paper submissions for 2026 have closed. Student registration rates are not shown on the main page.

title: SIGCSE Technical Symposium 2027 (Student Volunteers)
organizer_blurb: The ACM Special Interest Group on Computer Science Education.
summary: The largest ACM computing education conference. Student volunteers work up to 8 hours and get free base registration.
description: The SIGCSE Technical Symposium brings together computing educators and students for papers, panels, posters, workshops and the ACM Student Research Competition. Students can volunteer at the registration desk, check badges, help speakers and support online sessions, for up to 8 hours total. Volunteers get complimentary base registration, a SIGCSE student membership and the chance to meet students from other schools. Travel and hotel are not covered. The volunteer application was expected to open around November 2026, and organizers recommend applying early.
location: Sacramento, CA
dates_note: Student volunteer application expected to open around November 2026; no deadline posted. Poster and Student Research Competition submissions closed Sept 30, 2026.
pay: Free base registration for student volunteers; no travel or hotel funding
eligibility: Undergraduate or graduate students at a higher-education institution, at least 18 on the first conference day, registered as in-person attendees, with a sponsoring faculty member listed.

title: ACM CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems 2027
organizer_blurb: The ACM Special Interest Group on Computer-Human Interaction.
summary: The top international conference on human-computer interaction. Students can submit posters or a student research entry, or join as student volunteers.
description: CHI is the flagship HCI conference, with paper sessions, workshops, panels, interactive demos, posters and a Student Research Competition. Late-round tracks such as posters, interactive demos and the Student Research Competition are due Jan 21, 2027. CHI also runs a large student volunteer program; in 2026, volunteers worked at least 20 hours in exchange for waived registration and daily meals, applied through a lottery that ran from October to January, and covered their own travel and housing. Expect a similar process for 2027.
location: Pittsburgh, PA
dates_note: Deadline shown is for posters, interactive demos and the Student Research Competition. CHI 2027 student volunteer details are not posted yet; the 2026 lottery closed in late January.

title: Grace Hopper Celebration (GHC) 2026
organizer_blurb: A nonprofit that supports women and non-binary technologists and runs the Grace Hopper Celebration.
summary: A large annual conference for women and non-binary people in computing, known for its career expo and student recruiting.
description: GHC brings together students, researchers and industry leaders from around the world for keynotes, technical and career sessions, and networking with companies hiring in tech. The site links to awards and scholar programs and to a separate virtual GHC page. Pricing details were not posted when checked, so confirm costs and any scholarship options on the site before planning travel.
location: Anaheim, CA (Anaheim Convention Center)
dates_note: GHC 2027 dates and location are not yet announced. The pricing page was under construction when checked.

title: ACM Richard Tapia Celebration of Diversity in Computing 2027
organizer_blurb: CMD-IT (Center for Minorities and People with Disabilities in IT) co-sponsors the Tapia conference with ACM.
summary: A conference that celebrates diversity in computing, for undergraduate and graduate students, faculty, researchers and professionals.
description: Tapia brings together people in computing from all backgrounds, ethnicities and abilities. Students attend presentations and conversations with leaders who share their backgrounds, build community with peers that lasts beyond the conference, and get advice and contacts from people in academia and industry. The location changes from year to year; recent editions were in Grapevine, TX (2025) and Atlanta (2026).
dates_note: 2027 dates and location not yet announced; the 2026 edition ran Sept 16-18 in Atlanta. Join the mailing list on the site for updates.
eligibility: For undergraduate and graduate students, faculty, researchers and professionals in computing from all backgrounds.

title: SHPE National Convention 2027
organizer_blurb: A national organization supporting Hispanic students and professionals in STEM.
summary: SHPE's annual national convention, with hundreds of workshops, competitions and on-site recruiting for STEM students.
description: The SHPE National Convention combines hundreds of educational workshops and challenges, competitions with prize money, the STAR Awards, engagement and networking events, and on-site interviews that can lead to job offers. It draws students and professionals from across the country and is a major recruiting event for engineering and computing students.
location: Houston, TX
dates_note: The 2026 convention runs Oct 28-31, 2026 in Indianapolis. Registration costs are not shown on the event page.

title: PyCon US 2027
organizer_blurb: The nonprofit behind the Python language and the PyCon US conference.
summary: The largest annual gathering of the Python community, with a student rate and travel grants.
description: PyCon US runs about a week: paid tutorials, sponsor sessions, a three-day main conference of talks, a job fair and community showcase, then development sprints where attendees contribute to open source projects. Students get a reduced Student/Academic rate, and a travel grant program can help with flights, hotel and registration. The sprints are a good first step into open source contribution.
location: Long Beach, CA
dates_note: 2027 dates not yet announced; PyCon US 2026 ran May 13-19 in Long Beach, and 2027 is also planned for Long Beach. Check us.pycon.org for the 2027 call for proposals.
pay: Student rate was $139 in 2026 ($100 early bird); travel grants available
eligibility: The Student/Academic rate is for full-time students and academics.

title: IEEE VIS 2026
organizer: IEEE Visualization and Graphics Technical Community
organizer_blurb: IEEE VIS is the main academic conference for data visualization and visual analytics research.
summary: The top research conference for data visualization is in Copley Square this November. One-day student passes make it easy to drop in from Suffolk.
description: IEEE VIS 2026 runs November 9 to 13, 2026, with the main conference at The Westin Copley Place in Boston and satellites in Paris and Tianjin. Boston student rates are $599 full conference, $299 two-day, and $239 one-day for IEEE student members at the late rate, and $719, $359, and $289 for non-members. The early bird rate ended September 25, 2026. Student registrants attend the same papers, panels, and posters as everyone else. Refunds are available up to 30 days before the conference. A student volunteer program is not described on the registration page.
location: The Westin Copley Place, Boston, MA
dates_note: Monday to Friday. Late registration rates apply from September 26. Book the conference hotel by October 23 to keep the early bird hotel rate.
pay: $239 student one-day (IEEE member), $289 non-member; $599 student full conference (member)
eligibility: Student rates are for students; the page lists separate IEEE student member and non-member prices.

title: National Collegiate Research Conference (NCRC) 2027
organizer_blurb: HCURA is the Harvard student group that runs NCRC, a student-run undergraduate research conference.
summary: A student-run research conference at Harvard where undergraduates from any major present posters and talks. You do not need prior research to attend.
description: NCRC 2027 is January 22 to 24, 2027, at the Harvard University Northwest Building in Cambridge. HCURA describes it as the largest student-run research conference, with over 500 students from more than 100 universities. The weekend has poster sessions, oral presentations, keynote lectures, and panels, and it is fully in person. Applying costs $35, and accepted participants pay a $220 registration fee, which rises to $240 in the final week. The FAQ says students without prior research can still attend, and it suggests asking your school for travel or fee funding.
location: Harvard University Northwest Building, 52 Oxford St, Cambridge, MA
dates_note: Priority deadline November 22, 2026; regular deadline December 6, 2026; late deadline January 2, 2027 with a $20 late fee.
pay: $35 application fee; $220 registration if accepted ($240 in the final week)
eligibility: Undergraduates (freshman through senior) enrolled in a college or university at the time of the conference. Prior research is not required.

title: MIT Sloan Sports Analytics Conference (SSAC) 2027
organizer_blurb: SSAC is an annual MIT Sloan conference on data and analytics in the sports industry.
summary: The best-known sports analytics conference, held at the Seaport convention center. A good fit for data science students who want sports or media jobs.
description: SSAC27 runs February 25 and 26, 2027, at the Thomas M. Menino Convention and Exhibition Center in Boston, 7 AM to 5:30 PM both days. The program covers sports data, analytics, and business panels, and there is a research paper competition. The FAQ says a limited number of student tickets are sold each year and that buyers must be fully enrolled students at the time of the conference, with status verified. The 2027 student price is not shown on the pages we could read; tickets are sold through Eventbrite. Tickets are not sold during the conference, and refunds are available up to 30 days before.
location: Thomas M. Menino Convention and Exhibition Center, 415 Summer St, Boston, MA
dates_note: Thursday and Friday. Student tickets are limited each year; buy before the event since none are sold on site.
eligibility: Student tickets require full enrollment at the time of the conference and are subject to verification.

title: Emerging Technologies Student Leaders Conference 2027 (TechConnect World)
organizer_blurb: TechConnect runs the TechConnect World Innovation Conference on emerging technologies and commercialization.
summary: A student leaders program inside the TechConnect World conference in Boston. Accepted club leaders get free registration to the three-day conference.
description: The Student Leaders Conference runs March 23 to 25, 2027, in Boston as part of TechConnect World. It is aimed at undergraduate representatives of student groups in nano and emerging technologies, and the page says leaders from any science, technology, or business domain are welcome. Accepted applicants receive a registration waiver for the three-day conference, join the Student Leaders Program, and are named Emerging Technology Student Leader Awardees. The page does not give the venue name, the application deadline, or how to apply, and it does not mention travel support.
location: Boston, MA
dates_note: Application deadline and venue are not posted yet; check the TechConnect student page.
pay: Free registration waiver for accepted student leaders
eligibility: Undergraduate student group representatives; student leaders in any science, technology, or business domain.

title: Boston Application Security Conference (BASC) 2027
organizer_blurb: OWASP Boston is the local chapter of the Open Worldwide Application Security Project.
summary: A one-day application security conference run by OWASP Boston in Kendall Square. Useful for anyone interested in web security or secure coding.
description: BASC 2027 is a one-day conference on April 3, 2027, at the Boston Marriott Cambridge, from 8 AM to 6 PM. It has talks and workshops across Development, Leadership, and Research tracks, and it is organized by the OWASP Boston chapter. Ticket prices, any student rate, and the call for papers are not shown on the site yet.
location: Boston Marriott Cambridge, 50 Broadway, Cambridge, MA
dates_note: Saturday. Registration and pricing are not posted yet.
eligibility: Not stated on the page.

title: MinuteCon 2027
organizer_blurb: MinuteCon is a new independent hacker conference based in Boston.
summary: A new independent hacker conference in Cambridge with technical security research talks. The call for papers and upcoming volunteer call are good ways for students to get involved.
description: MinuteCon 2027 is planned for April 30 and May 1, 2027, at the Boston Marriott Cambridge, with about 500 attendees. Talks cover offensive security, defense and detection, application security, hardware, AI security, and policy. The call for papers is open on Sessionize until January 15, 2027, with 20-minute and 45-minute slots, and accepted speakers get free admission. Early bird tickets sold out; Round 2 tickets and a Call for Volunteers are listed as upcoming. Ticket prices and any student rate are not posted.
location: Boston Marriott Cambridge, 50 Broadway, Cambridge, MA
dates_note: Friday and Saturday. The deadline shown is the call for papers. Round 2 tickets and volunteer signups are not open yet.
eligibility: Not stated on the page.

title: ODSC AI East 2027
organizer_blurb: ODSC runs applied data science and AI conferences in the US and Europe.
summary: A large applied AI and data science conference at the Seaport. The free Expo pass is the easy way in for students.
description: ODSC AI East 2027 runs May 10 to 12, 2027, at the Menino Convention and Exhibition Center in Boston. The Expo pass is free by application or $99 guaranteed and covers two days of the expo hall, keynotes, and builder demos. Paid passes start at $359 for Learn and $999 for Build, and virtual tiers run from free to $249. The 2027 page does not list a student discount; the 2026 discount page offered students 10% off with proof of enrollment. A volunteer program is not mentioned.
location: Menino Convention and Exhibition Center, Boston, MA
dates_note: Monday to Wednesday. Prices rise in rounds; no fixed deadline is posted.
pay: Free Expo pass by application ($99 guaranteed); paid passes from $359
eligibility: Not stated on the page.

title: CSAW 2026 (Cyber Security Awareness Worldwide)
organizer_blurb: CSAW is a student-run cybersecurity games and conference event hosted by NYU Tandon.
summary: The largest student-focused cybersecurity games and conference in the US, run out of NYU Tandon in Brooklyn. Worth a trip for CTF players and anyone curious about security research.
description: CSAW 2026 runs November 12 to 14, 2026, in person, with the US-Canada final hosted by NYU Tandon in Brooklyn. It combines a conference with twelve competitions, including Capture The Flag, the Embedded Security Challenge, Hack My Robot, the LLM CTF Attack Competition, the Quantum Security Challenge, and the Cyber Policy Competition. Participants range from high school to doctoral students. US-Canada registration is through a Google Form linked on the page. The page does not state cost, the exact venue room, or eligibility rules, and most competition finals require qualifying in earlier rounds.
location: NYU Tandon School of Engineering, 370 Jay St, Brooklyn, NY
dates_note: Thursday to Saturday. Check each competition's page for finalist rules.
eligibility: Participants range from high school to doctoral students; specific eligibility is not stated on the page.

title: BSides Philadelphia 2026
organizer_blurb: BSides Philadelphia is a volunteer-run community cybersecurity conference.
summary: A one-day community security conference in South Philly with talks, workshops, and a CTF. Easy Amtrak trip and friendly to students.
description: BSides Philadelphia 2026 is on Friday, December 11, 2026, from 8 AM to 6 PM at Live! Casino and Hotel Philadelphia. The program includes talks, workshops, CTF competitions, and networking. The organizers describe it as volunteer-run for security practitioners, researchers, and students. It is a paid event, but ticket prices and any student rate are not shown in the page text.
location: Live! Casino & Hotel Philadelphia, 900 Packer Ave, Philadelphia, PA
dates_note: Friday, 8 AM to 6 PM.
eligibility: Not stated on the page.

title: CCSC Northeastern Conference (CCSCNE) 2027
organizer: Consortium for Computing Sciences in Colleges, Northeast Region
organizer_blurb: CCSCNE is the northeast regional arm of CCSC and runs an annual CS education conference with ACM SIGCSE.
summary: A regional CS conference in New Hampshire with an undergraduate poster competition and a programming contest. Cheap student registration and a short drive from Boston.
description: The 31st CCSC Northeastern Conference is April 2 and 3, 2027, at Southern New Hampshire University in Manchester, NH. It is a refereed CS education conference held in cooperation with ACM SIGCSE. Undergraduates can submit a 300-word abstract to the Undergraduate Poster Exhibit and Research/Application Development Competition, which needs a faculty sponsor; judges award prizes to the top three posters. A programming contest takes teams of up to three undergraduates for $280 per team with a faculty advisor. Student registration is $75 through March 21, 2027 and $85 after, and includes the Friday banquet; lunch is not provided. The 2027 poster deadline is not posted yet.
location: Southern New Hampshire University, Manchester, NH
dates_note: Friday and Saturday. The deadline shown is early registration; the poster abstract deadline is not posted yet.
eligibility: Undergraduate posters need a faculty sponsor and graduate students may not author them. Programming contest teams are up to three undergraduates with a registered faculty advisor.

title: PyData Global 2026
organizer_blurb: PyData is a NumFOCUS program of community conferences on open source data tools.
summary: A two-day online PyData conference with pay-what-you-can tickets. A low-cost way to hear data science and Python talks from home.
description: PyData Global 2026 is a virtual conference on December 9 and 10, 2026, with live keynotes, talks, and lightning talks. Tickets are sold as a recommended donation based on your country, with a $50 student tier and $100 individual tier for the US, and you can adjust the amount. The site does not list financial aid or a volunteer program on the pages we read.
location: Remote (online)
dates_note: Wednesday and Thursday, online across time zones.
pay: $50 suggested student donation (pay what you can)
eligibility: Not stated on the page.

title: GitHub Universe 2026
organizer_blurb: GitHub is the code hosting platform owned by Microsoft.
summary: GitHub's developer conference in San Francisco next week. The virtual pass is free, so anyone can watch keynotes and sessions.
description: GitHub Universe 2026 runs October 28 and 29, 2026, at Fort Mason Center in San Francisco, with in-person and virtual options. The virtual pass is free and includes streamed keynotes and recorded sessions. In-person passes cost $1,399, and add-ons include a $99 workshop and a $30 certification voucher. The page does not mention a student discount.
location: Fort Mason Center, San Francisco, CA
dates_note: Wednesday and Thursday. October 27 is invitation-only and the October 30 Day of Learning is sold out.
eligibility: Not stated on the page.

title: AfroTech Conference 2026
organizer_blurb: AfroTech is a conference and media brand focused on Black professionals in technology.
summary: A large conference for Black technologists in Houston with sessions, recruiting, and networking. Some sessions are marked for students.
description: AfroTech 2026 runs November 2 to 6, 2026, at the George R. Brown Convention Center in Houston. The Premier four-day pass is $625, Executive is $850, and All Access is $2,250, and a one-day AI Virtual Training is $97. The page shows Student as an eligible pass type for some sessions, such as a tech career session, but it does not list a student ticket price or a student program.
location: George R. Brown Convention Center, Houston, TX
dates_note: Monday to Friday.
pay: $625 Premier pass; no student price listed
eligibility: Not stated on the page.

title: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026
organizer_blurb: CNCF is the Linux Foundation project that hosts Kubernetes and other cloud native open source projects.
summary: The main Kubernetes and cloud native conference, with a cheap academic rate for full-time students. Good for anyone into DevOps or cloud.
description: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 runs November 9 to 12, 2026, at the Salt Palace Convention Center in Salt Lake City, with co-located AI and agentics days on November 9. The academic rate for full-time students, faculty, and staff is $200 for KubeCon only and $275 for All-Access, plus 8.45% sales tax. You must upload a dated student ID, a current class transcript, or proof of employment. The scholarship page we found shows only an old closed cycle, so no open scholarship is confirmed for this event.
location: Salt Palace Convention Center, Salt Lake City, UT
dates_note: Monday to Thursday. Late registration runs through November 12; the refund cutoff is October 26 with a 6% fee.
pay: $200 academic (KubeCon only); $275 academic All-Access, plus tax
eligibility: Academic rate requires current full-time student, faculty, or staff status with an institution ID, transcript, or proof of employment.

title: NeurIPS 2026
organizer_blurb: NeurIPS is one of the largest annual research conferences in machine learning.
summary: The biggest machine learning research conference, this year in Sydney with a satellite site in Atlanta. Students get a lower full-time student rate.
description: NeurIPS 2026 runs December 6 to 12 in Sydney (main site), with satellite sites in Atlanta and Paris on December 9 to 13. Student registration requires full-time enrollment in an accredited program and proof of enrollment at check-in. Early pricing ends October 31, 2026, and full refunds end November 4. Financial assistance and volunteer applications for Sydney and Atlanta closed October 6, so only regular registration is still open. The pricing page did not show the student price in text.
location: Sydney, Australia (main); satellite sites in Atlanta, GA and Paris, France
dates_note: Sydney December 6 to 12; Atlanta and Paris December 9 to 13. The deadline shown is the end of early pricing.
eligibility: Student registrants must be full-time students in an accredited program and present proof of enrollment.

title: AAAI-27 Conference and Student Scholar Volunteer Program
organizer: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI)
organizer_blurb: AAAI is a scientific society that runs one of the major AI research conferences.
summary: A major AI research conference in Montreal, with a volunteer program that gives undergraduates free registration and some travel support.
description: AAAI-27 runs February 16 to 23, 2027, in Montreal. The Student Scholar Volunteer Program is open to full-time undergraduate and graduate students who are AAAI members, have submitted a paper to the conference, and have a faculty recommendation letter; local students may volunteer if spots remain. Scholars get partial travel support, and volunteers get complimentary technical program registration. Applications open November 30 and close December 4, 2026. Do not register before you hear back, or you lose the free registration. The Undergraduate Consortium and student abstract deadlines have already passed.
location: Montreal, QC, Canada
dates_note: Volunteer applications open November 30, 2026 at 12:01 AM ET and close December 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET.
pay: Free registration for volunteers; partial travel support for scholars
eligibility: Full-time undergraduate or graduate students, AAAI members, who submitted a paper to AAAI-27 and have a faculty recommendation letter. Local students may apply to volunteer if openings remain.

title: Emerging Researchers National (ERN) Conference in STEM 2027
organizer: Emerging Researchers National (ERN) Conference in STEM
organizer_blurb: ERN is a national conference where undergraduate and graduate students present STEM research.
summary: A national student research conference in Atlanta where undergrads present posters or talks. Travel awards are offered.
description: The 2027 ERN Conference in STEM runs March 4 to 6, 2027, at the Hyatt Regency Atlanta. It is aimed at college and university undergraduate and graduate students in any STEMM field. Based on last year's rules, students doing research in the US can be primary author on one poster or oral abstract, with mentor approval. The 2027 abstract deadline and travel award details are not posted yet. General registration closes December 4, 2026.
location: Hyatt Regency Atlanta, 265 Peachtree Rd NE, Atlanta, GA
dates_note: Thursday to Saturday. The deadline shown is the close of general registration; the abstract deadline is not posted yet.
eligibility: College and university undergraduate and graduate students in STEMM. Abstract rules (2026 version) require US-based research and mentor approval.

title: WiCyS 2027 Conference
organizer_blurb: WiCyS is a nonprofit that supports the recruitment and advancement of women in cybersecurity.
summary: The main women in cybersecurity conference, with a student poster session and scholarships that cover registration and lodging.
description: WiCyS 2027 runs March 17 to 19, 2027, at the Gaylord Rockies Resort and Convention Center near Denver. Student scholarships cover registration, meals, and two nights of shared lodging for a $75 processing fee, with a few $500 travel stipends; applications closed September 30 and results come November 18, 2026. Students without a scholarship can use limited open registration, which opens December 9, 2026. Student poster submissions are due November 4, 2026 at 5 PM CT. A virtual edition is also planned.
location: Gaylord Rockies Resort & Convention Center, Aurora, CO
dates_note: The deadline shown is student posters. Scholarship decisions arrive November 18; general registration opens December 9, 2026.
pay: Scholarship covers registration and shared lodging for a $75 fee
eligibility: Scholarships are open to all WiCyS member types. Students without a scholarship may use limited open registration.

title: National Conference on Undergraduate Research (NCUR) 2027
organizer_blurb: CUR supports undergraduate research and runs NCUR each year.
summary: The largest national undergraduate research conference, open to any major. A good first place to present a class or lab project.
description: NCUR 2027 runs April 12 to 14, 2027, at DeVos Place Convention Center in Grand Rapids, Michigan, with Grand Valley State University. The abstract portal is open until December 4, 2026, and decisions come January 13, 2027. Registration opens January 13 with an early-bird deadline of January 29. The primary presenter must be an undergraduate researcher, international and two-year college students are eligible, and CUR membership is not required. Registration fees depend on your school's CUR membership and are not listed on the pages we read.
